title: I Used the Chart-Room Camera Through Three Request Days After They Cut the Slot

parts.text: I booked the chart room at 11:04 a.m. and intern Jules had already cut my numbered slot. The board said: ONE SLOT. REQUESTS STAY ON CAMERA. I was thirty-four, archive steward, holding a slip that listed our plate. Jules shrugged. "Interns are the room." I photographed the board, the cut, and his hands on my plate. Then I asked for the camera. At 11:12 the desk pinged a request with no slot.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The camera just logged a request with no numbered slot.

social.video_title: They cut my chart-room slot and pulled the plate — Part 1/3
social.description: Chart room, a cut slot, hands on my plate. Would you have asked for the camera?

parts.text: Tuesday they pulled the next plate. I printed Monday's still and taped it to the board. Jules called it research. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. The board now has the still. At 11:18 the desk asked why the camera showed two plates on a cut slot. Jules said optics. Optics is a word interns use when a request exists.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They pulled the next plate; the board now has the still.

social.video_title: The camera showed two plates on a cut slot — Part 2/3
social.description: Second plate, a still on the board, a cut slot. Was research ever a booking?

parts.text: Thursday the board added a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE ROOM. Jules ran his own slot and told the next intern atmosphere was always about optics. I keep our plates on a labeled cart. The camera logs every request. Jules brown-bags his research. The room finally looks like a slot, not a cut. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Interns are not the room — Part 3/3
social.description: Second line on the board, labeled cart, camera on every request. Was research ever a cut slot?
